basis: the fleet, component types, capacities, spare parts and initial ages are AVR-04's main instance (pmo v1.0.0, generate_instance, 10 aircraft x 4 types x 52 weeks); its Weibull scales and maximum intervals, given in weeks at a known schedule, are converted to flight hours at the design utilization of 800 FH a year, so at mean use the two projects coincide exactly

illustrative assumption: each task is due at its FH limit or at a calendar limit 50 % longer than the FH limit lasts at mean use, whichever comes first ('FH or months, whichever first' is the usual form of a maintenance programme's interval)

illustrative assumption: a task forced because a component reached its FH limit before its planned week grounds the aircraft outside a planned slot; the operator must cover owner flights with supplemental charter, priced at 2.5 times AVR-04's 20 000 $ planned aircraft-week
numerical: an age within this relative tolerance of the FH limit counts as within it, so a component flown at exactly the design rate is never forced by rounding in a cumulative sum
